newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Wednesday with funds on the market gradually increasing due to the current peak of state debt redemption, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose to 7.99 percent from 6.50 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 3.5 million lots from 5.8 million.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said liquidity was growing as funds released by the redemption of state debt entered the repo market.
"Big institutions are now unwilling to borrow money through the repo market," one trader said. "They have plenty of funds as a result of the redemptions."
But the bullish domestic A share markets supported the early-maturing contracts on Wednesday, especially the three-day contract, traders said.
They said they expected the rates to continue to move in a narrow range on Thursday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended up across the board on Wednesday led by the market leader, the three-year note which matures in August 1999, traders said.
The three-year note closed up 0.22 yuan at 106.90 yuan after hitting a year high price of 107.5 yuan in intra-day trading.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 118.79 yuan from 118.09 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose sharply to 2.1 million lots from 1.2 million lots.
Traders said they believed the spot contracts would continue to rise in the next few days due to the extra liquidity on the market, also derived from the redemption of state debt.
